name: Yaroslav and Two Strings
description: Yaroslav thinks that two strings s and w , consisting of digits and having length n are non-comparable if there are two numbers, i and j (1 ≤ i , j ≤ n ) , such that s i > w i and s j < w j . Here sign s i represents the i -th digit of string s , similarly, w j represents the j -th digit of string w . A string's template is a string that consists of digits and question marks (" ? "). Yaroslav has two string templates, each of them has length n . Yaroslav wants to count the number of ways to replace all question marks by some integers in both templates, so as to make the resulting strings incomparable. Note that the obtained strings can contain leading zeroes and that distinct question marks can be replaced by distinct or the same integers. Help Yaroslav, calculate the remainder after dividing the described number of ways by 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) .
input_specification: The first line contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) — the length of both templates. The second line contains the first template — a string that consists of digits and characters " ? ". The string's length equals n . The third line contains the second template in the same format.
output_specification: In a single line print the remainder after dividing the answer to the problem by number 1000000007 (10 9 + 7) .
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 296B — Yaroslav and Two Strings [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
